summary.title: Tutorial: Finding Important Words in Text Using TF-IDF
summary.one_liner: You learn how TF-IDF scores words by in-document frequency versus rarity across a set of documents, and how to implement it in about 14 lines of Python with TextBlob.
keywords: how to find key terms in a document
takeaways: TF-IDF multiplies term frequency (normalized word count in a document) by inverse document frequency (log of total documents over documents containing the word).
Common words that appear across many documents get a low score, while words frequent in one document get a high score.
The article gives a working Python implementation using TextBlob with tf, n_containing, idf and tfidf functions.
A sample run over three Wikipedia-based documents shows top words per document, such as 'films' and 'genus'.
The author notes possible improvements such as stopword removal or a different tf scheme, left to the reader.
summary.summary: The author introduces TF-IDF (Term Frequency, Inverse Document Frequency) as a way to score how important a word is within a document relative to a collection of documents. The post walks through four small Python functions (tf, n_containing, idf, tfidf) built on TextBlob, then applies them to three short Wikipedia-derived texts about Python topics. It prints the top three scored words for each document and points out possible refinements like stopword filtering. The page also includes edit notes for TextBlob import and bug fixes and a few further reading links.
